title: Customer-segment PPK variance and cache impact analysis
content:
Executive summary:

This workbook explores per-customer-segment variability in per-paid-token (PPK) economics for Hosted API, and quantifies the impact of prefix/KV cache hit rates across sequence-length distributions and regions. Aim: create a prioritized, low-effort set of optimizations (routing, cache TTL, prewarm, pricing tiers) that recover 8–20% of marginal COGS for mid/high volume segments without degrading 99th percentile latency SLAs.

Why this matters:
- Large variance in observed PPK across customers is driven by three confirmed levers: sequence length mix, cache effectiveness (cold vs warm prefixes), and model family selection (fp16 vs int8 variants).
- Small changes in cache hit rate produce outsized token savings for high-traffic short-sequence workloads (chat, search snippets).
- Current telemetry lacks productized per-customer PPK dashboards; this sheet is a hypothesis-first workbook to guide which metrics and instrumentation to build next.

Key assumptions used in the model (base case):
- Regional infra cost: US-west GPU-hour effective cost = $2.25 (amortized + infra); EU-west = $2.60.
- Model families considered: rwd-1-large (base perf), rwd-1-quant-int8 (30% token cost improvement on long seqs), open-llama-70B (higher cost per token due to memory pressure).
- Average tokens per request: segment A (chat-heavy) = 220, segment B (search) = 48, segment C (batch summarization) = 880.
- Baseline batching efficiency: 1.85x for short seq, 2.6x for long seq workloads.
- Cache hit rate scenarios: cold=5%, current=22%, warmed=55% (prefix/KV cache effectiveness).

Sheet layout and tabs (what to open):
- "Overview_Summaries": one-line KPIs and scenario snapshots by segment.
- "PerRequest_COGS_Model": per-token cost calc by region/model/quantization under different seq lengths and batch factors.
- "CacheSensitivity": matrix of PPK vs cache-hit% by segment and model family.
- "Routing_Impact": simulated routing policies (latency-first, cost-first, hybrid) and their impact on PPK and 99p latency.
- "ActionTracker": prioritized actions, expected savings, required owners and engineering effort estimate (T-shirt).

Sample rows from PerRequest_COGS_Model (CSV-style for quick copy):
Segment,Region,Model,SeqLen,BatchFactor,CacheHit,TokensPerReq,TokensServedPerReq,PerTokenCostUSD,PPKUSD
chat-A,us-west,rwd-1-large,220,1.9,0.22,220,171.6,0.0000185,0.0031766
search-B,us-west,rwd-1-quant-int8,48,2.0,0.55,48,21.6,0.0000122,0.0002635
batch-C,eu-west,open-llama-70B,880,2.6,0.05,880,836.0,0.0000254,0.0212344

Interpretation notes on table: tokens served per request = tokens per req * (1 - cache_hit) + baseline_kv_overhead. Per-token cost is model+infra normalized per token after batching and amortized GPU usage; numbers are illustrative and based on infra benchmarks from Aug–Sep 2025.

CacheSensitivity tab takeaways (high level):
- For chat-A (short-medium seq): increasing cache hit from 22% to 55% reduces PPK by ~14–17% depending on model family. This is primarily because short prefixes are disproportionately repeated and benefit from prefix KV caching.
- For batch-C (long seq): cache moves the needle less on PPK (<6%) because inference cost dominated by generation tokens, not prefix re-use.
- Region matters: EU-west per-token baseline is ~12% higher than US-west due to infrastructure pricing and exchange impacts; caching yields slightly higher relative savings in EU-west since fixed infra overhead is greater.

Sensitivity snapshots (three scenarios, aggregated across segments):
- Best case (aggressive caching + int8 rollout): PPK reduction = 19% relative to baseline; margin uplift = +8–12 ppts for hosted API SKU.
- Base case (current caching + measured batching): PPK reduction = 6%; margin uplift = +2–4 ppts.
- Worst case (cold caches during surges + heavier long-tail sequences): PPK increases 4–7%; margin compresses -1–3 ppts.

Routing_Impact simulation summary:
- Latency-first routing (route to closest region + lowest model-latency variant) keeps 99p latency within target for high-SLA customers but increases PPK for heavy short-sequence traffic by ~9% versus cost-first baseline.
- Cost-first routing (route by lowest estimated PPK across compatible model variants) can save ~6–12% PPK across mid-volume segments but requires strict SLA guardrails and fallback rules for spikes.
- Hybrid policy (prefer cost unless predicted 99p latency > threshold) recovers most savings (~8–10%) while keeping 99p within 1.2x target in simulations.

Concrete recommendations and estimated impact (ordered):
1) Build a per-tenant PPK dashboard (product + telemetry) — expected 0% engineering complexity, high visibility. Owner: Sofia Li. Impact: immediate ability to triage top 30% of PPK variance.
2) Short-term ops: increase default prefix cache TTL from 20s to 60s for chat-like routes; monitor 99p latency for cold starts — low effort (SRE change). Estimated savings: 5–9% PPK for affected customers. Owner: Marina Petrova.
3) Medium-term: rollout int8 quantized model variants for eligible workloads with auto-fallback to fp16 when quality regressions detected. Effort: medium (compiler + eval infra). Impact: 12–18% PPK improvement on long sequences, 6–10% on short. Owner: Eng-Serving runtime (Ravi Menon coordinating).
4) Routing experiments: create two A/B experiments for hybrid routing (cost-hybrid) vs latency-first. Run for 4 weeks on 5% traffic with strict rollback hooks. Owner: Jordan Kim. Expected: net platform saving 6–9% PPK if stable.
5) Pricing/design: introduce a "warm-cache" SLA add-on for high-volume customers (>1M req/day) at a small premium if they want guaranteed warmed prefixes (pre-warm + reserved pool). Impact: monetizable improvement and predictable capacity. Owner: Product-Hosted API.

Instrumentation and further data we need (prioritized):
- Per-request: include model-variant-id, region, observed batch-size, cache_hit_boolean, prefix_hash.
- Per-tenant rolling window: PPK, median/99p latency, seqLen distribution, percent of requests eligible for int8 variant.
- Event markers: cache-eviction events, instance pre-warm triggers, model-fallbacks.

ActionTracker (short entries):
- [Sofia] Build PPK dashboard prototype — due 2025-10-09 — depends on adding per-request fields (low effort).
- [Marina] TTL change and monitoring alarm — due 2025-10-02 — quick rollback plan in place.
- [Ravi] Coordinate int8 experimental rollout — kickoff 2025-10-12, milestone: internal evals 2025-11-06.
- [Jordan] Launch routing A/B: design by 2025-10-20, run start 2025-11-01.

Open questions / risks:
- Quality regressions for int8 on some prompts: need human eval sampling and automatic quality gates (we have a prototype eval harness, see linked PR).
- Edge-case customers with extremely bursty traffic could see cache churn; TTL increase might harm memory footprint or eviction rates.
- Observability gap: without prefix_hash surfaced we cannot confidently attribute cache hits to repeating prefixes vs accidental collisions.

Appendix (quick formulas used):
- TokensServedPerReq = tokens_per_req * (1 - cache_hit) + kv_overhead_tokens
- EffectiveBatchFactor adjusted by seqLen and concurrency; PerTokenCostUSD = (amortized_gpu_cost_per_second * avg_inference_seconds_per_req) / (tokens_served_per_req * average_batch_factor) + model_kernel_penalty

Notes to reviewers: please comment inline on the ActionTracker where you think customer-level rollout should be gated (by PPK threshold, by SLA, or by volume). This is intentionally pragmatic — we want some low-friction plays we can push to production quickly, and a medium-term plan that ties to int8 and routing changes.
